Maximum Static Friction & Angle of Repose

fs,max⁡=μsN,tan⁡θr=μsf_{s,\max} = \mu_s N, \quad \tan \theta_r = \mu_sfs,max​=μs​N,tanθr​=μs​

Static friction self-adjusts up to its limiting value fs,max⁡f_{s,\max}fs,max​. Once the component of external force along the contact plane exceeds this threshold, relative sliding initiates. The angle of repose θr\theta_rθr​ is the maximum angle of an inclined plane at which a block placed on it remains in equilibrium without sliding.

Variable Conventions
fs,max⁡f_{s,\max}fs,max​: Limiting (maximum) static frictional force (Newtons)
μs\mu_sμs​: Coefficient of static friction between surfaces (dimensionless)
NNN: Normal contact force exerted perpendicular to the surface
θr\theta_rθr​: Angle of repose of the inclined plane

Work-Kinetic Energy Theorem

Wtotal=Wc+Wnc+Wext=ΔK=12mvf2−12mvi2W_{\text{total}} = W_c + W_{nc} + W_{\text{ext}} = \Delta K = \frac{1}{2}m v_f^2 - \frac{1}{2}m v_i^2Wtotal​=Wc​+Wnc​+Wext​=ΔK=21​mvf2​−21​mvi2​

The total work performed on a particle by all forces (conservative, non-conservative, and external forces combined) equals the net change in its kinetic energy in an inertial reference frame.

Variable Conventions
WtotalW_{\text{total}}Wtotal​: Net algebraic work done by all acting forces (Joules)
WcW_cWc​: Work done by conservative forces ($-\Delta U$)
WncW_{nc}Wnc​: Work done by non-conservative forces such as friction
ΔK\Delta KΔK: Change in translational kinetic energy

Ceq=ε0A∑diKi=ε0Ad1K1+d2K2C_{eq} = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{\sum \frac{d_i}{K_i}} = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{\frac{d_1}{K_1} + \frac{d_2}{K_2}}Ceq​=∑Ki​di​​ε0​A​=K1​d1​​+K2​d2​​ε0​A​

When dielectric slabs are stacked parallel to the plates, the electric field is modified in each segment, equivalent to individual capacitors connected in series with common charge QQQ.

did_idi​: Thickness of dielectric layer $i$

Shortest Distance Between Two Skew Lines

d=∣(a⃗2−a⃗1)⋅(b⃗1×b⃗2)∣∣b⃗1×b⃗2∣d = \frac{\left| (\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1) \cdot (\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2) \right|}{\left| \vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2 \right|}d=​b1​×b2​​​(a2​−a1​)⋅(b1​×b2​)​​

For two non-parallel, non-intersecting lines in three-dimensional space r⃗1=a⃗1+λb⃗1\vec{r}_1 = \vec{a}_1 + \lambda \vec{b}_1r1​=a1​+λb1​ and r⃗2=a⃗2+μb⃗2\vec{r}_2 = \vec{a}_2 + \mu \vec{b}_2r2​=a2​+μb2​, the shortest distance is the projection of vector joining their position vectors onto the common perpendicular unit normal.

Variable Conventions
a⃗1,a⃗2\vec{a}_1, \vec{a}_2a1​,a2​: Position vectors of arbitrary known points lying on line 1 and 2
b⃗1,b⃗2\vec{b}_1, \vec{b}_2b1​,b2​: Direction vectors of line 1 and line 2
b⃗1×b⃗2\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2b1​×b2​: Vector mutually perpendicular to both lines

King's Rule in Definite Integration

∫abf(x)dx=∫abf(a+b−x)dx\int_{a}^{b} f(x) dx = \int_{a}^{b} f(a + b - x) dx∫ab​f(x)dx=∫ab​f(a+b−x)dx

A fundamental symmetry property of Riemann integrals. It allows simplification of trigonometric and symmetric polynomial integrands by adding the transformed integral to the original integral.

Variable Conventions
a,ba, ba,b: Lower and upper limits of definite integration
f(x)f(x)f(x): Continuous integrand function on $[a, b]$
